perspective:
Sara’s available information:

- She knows herself as Sara Manuelito, a Speech-Language Pathologist. She knows Shirley Whiteplume as a nurse, long-time colleague, and close friend at the community health center.
- She attended the funeral of a mutual patient. She directly observed Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- She heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept thinking whether more could have been done. Sara told Shirley they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought. Shirley said it was hard to let go.
- At a work coffee break, Sara raised their treatment decisions and said she sensed Shirley felt burdened. She heard Shirley say she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have given him a better chance. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had. Shirley said she appreciated that but found it hard to accept.
- During a quiet office moment, Sara observed Shirley being reserved and minimally expressive. Sara confronted her about holding back feelings. Shirley said she didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said expressing emotions is healthy and not weak, especially among friends. Shirley said Sara might be right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, Sara felt her confrontation may have been too harsh and apologized. Shirley said it was a bit much but that Sara meant well and she appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley. Shirley thanked her and said talking helps.
- Later, Sara observed Shirley seemed to be doing better and asked how she was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley said she would like that and suggested planning something for the weekend.
